# Copilot Instructions — My Knowledge Board

## What this project is

My Knowledge Board is a multi-tenant internal knowledge platform (MERN stack). Organizations manage internal documentation through a role-based approval workflow. An AI chatbot (Google Gemini) answers questions about company policies.

---

## Repository layout

```
my-knowledge-board/
├── client/          # React 19 + Vite frontend
│   └── src/
│       ├── App.jsx              # Route definitions and route guards
│       ├── components/          # Feature-based UI (each folder has .jsx + .css)
│       ├── contexts/            # AppProvider, AuthProvider, FetcherProvider, etc.
│       └── hooks/               # useAuth, useCompany, useFetcher, useSocket
├── server/          # Node.js + Express backend (ESM)
│   ├── server.js    # Entry: DB connect, Socket.IO setup, HTTP listen
│   ├── app.js       # Middleware stack + route mounting
│   ├── controllers/ # Business logic (one file per domain)
│   ├── models/      # Mongoose schemas
│   ├── routes/      # Thin route modules
│   ├── middleware/  # protect/admin/manager auth, errorHandler, cloudinary, moderation
│   └── utils/       # generateToken, sendEmail
└── package.json     # Root scripts (install-all, dev, format)
```

---

## Key commands

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Install all dependencies | `npm run install-all` (root) |
| Start dev (frontend + backend) | `npm run dev` (root) |
| Start frontend only | `npm run dev --prefix client` |
| Start backend only | `npm run dev --prefix server` |
| Run client tests | `npm run test --prefix client` |
| Run server tests | `npm run test --prefix server` |
| Lint client | `npm run lint --prefix client` |
| Format all code | `npm run format` (root) |

**Errors & workarounds:**
- Both client and server use `"type": "module"` (ESM). Never use `require()`.
- The server loads env vars via `nodemon -r dotenv/config server.js` in dev. In production it uses `node -r dotenv/config server.js`. Always have a `server/.env` before starting.
- The client Vitest config uses `happy-dom` as the environment; tests that need full DOM APIs may need `jsdom` explicitly.

## Core architectural patterns

### Multi-tenancy
- Every user has a `companyId` field that is **an array** of ObjectIds (users can belong to multiple workspaces).
- All data queries must scope to `companyId: { $in: req.user.companyId }` — never a single-value equality check.

### RBAC
- `req.user.role` is **an array** of strings: `['Employee']`, `['Manager']`, `['Admin']`.
- Always check membership, not equality:
  ```js
  req.user.role.includes('Admin')   // ✅
  req.user.role === 'Admin'         // ❌
  ```
- Middleware: `protect` (any auth), `manager` (Manager or Admin), `admin` (Admin only) — from `server/middleware/authMiddleware.js`.

### Authentication
- JWT stored in an **httpOnly cookie** named `jwt`. Never expose it to client-side JS.
- Token generated with `generateToken(res, userId)` from `server/utils/generateToken.js`.
- Cookie settings: `secure: true` and `sameSite: 'none'` in production; `lax` in dev.

### Controller pattern (backend)
- All controllers are wrapped with `express-async-handler` — no try/catch boilerplate.
- Error pattern: set status code first, then throw:
  ```js
  res.status(404);
  throw new Error('Article not found');
  ```
- Global error handler at `server/middleware/errorHandler.js` formats the response.
- JSDoc comment block before each controller:
  ```js
  // @desc    Brief description
  // @route   METHOD /api/path
  // @access  Public | Private | Private (Manager/Admin)
  ```

### Article lifecycle
Status flow: `Draft` → `Pending` → `Approved` or `Rejected`.
- New articles created by employees default to `Pending` (skip Draft).
- Managers/Admins can approve/reject via `PATCH /api/articles/:id/status`.
- Articles expire after 180 days; managers certify them via `PATCH /api/articles/:id/certify`.

### Vector search (duplicate detection)
- Articles store a `contentEmbedding` (array of floats, hidden by default via `select: false`).
- Embeddings generated by `generateEmbedding()` in `server/controllers/aiController.js` using Google Gemini.
- Duplicate check uses MongoDB Atlas `$vectorSearch` aggregation with index name `vector_index`.
- A score > 0.85 is considered a likely duplicate.

### Real-time (Socket.IO)
- Server creates rooms per user: `join_user_room` event with `userId`.
- Client connects via `SocketProvider`; access via `useSocket()` hook.
- Notifications are pushed over sockets and persisted in `models/Notification.js`.

## Frontend patterns

### Component conventions
- Feature-based folders: each component lives in its own directory with a `.jsx` file and a co-located `.css` file (kebab-case name matching the component, e.g., `ArticleCard.jsx` + `article-card.css`).
- No TypeScript — plain JS/JSX throughout.
- No `prop-types` enforcement (`"react/prop-types": "off"` in ESLint).

### State management
Contexts are composed in `AppProvider.jsx` in this dependency order:
1. `FetcherProvider` (base HTTP utility)
2. `AuthProvider` (depends on Fetcher)
3. `SocketProvider` (depends on Auth)
4. `CompanyProvider` (depends on Auth)

Access via hooks: `useAuth()`, `useCompany()`, `useFetcher()`, `useSocket()`.

### Routing and guards
- `App.jsx` defines all routes.
- `ProtectedRoute` — any authenticated user.
- `AdminRoute` — Manager or Admin roles only.

### API calls
Use `useFetcher()` for all HTTP requests — it handles credentials and error interception. Do not use raw `fetch` or `axios` directly in components.

### Rich text
Articles use TinyMCE (`@tinymce/tinymce-react`) for content editing. The editor API key is provided via `VITE_TINYMCE_API_KEY`.

---

## Code style

- **Formatter**: Prettier — single quotes, semicolons, trailing commas (ES5), 80-char print width.
- **ESLint**: flat config (`eslint.config.js` in client). React hooks rules enforced.
- **Modules**: ESM (`import`/`export`) everywhere — both client and server.
- Husky + lint-staged run Prettier on staged files before commits.

---

## Testing

Both client and server use **Vitest**.

### Server tests (`server/__tests__/` and `server/tests/`)
- Use `vi.mock()` to isolate Mongoose models and external services.
- `makeRes()` helper pattern: manually constructed response object with `vi.fn()` spies.
- `run(controller, req, res)` helper drives `asyncHandler`-wrapped controllers to completion.
- Tests live alongside the `__tests__` directory; some are in `tests/`.

### Client tests (`client/src/**/__tests__/` or co-located)
- `@testing-library/react` + Vitest.
- Run with `npm run test --prefix client`.

## API surface (quick reference)

| Route prefix | Domain |
|---|---|
| `/api/auth` | Login, register, logout, forgot password |
| `/api/companies` | Tenant workspace registration + listing |
| `/api/users` | Profile, directory, managers, favorites |
| `/api/articles` | Full article CRUD + approval + search |
| `/api/ai` | Embedding generation, vector search |
| `/api/chat` | AI chatbot (Gemini) |
| `/api/notifications` | User notification records |
| `/api/sessions` | Admin session log access |

---

## Data model quick reference

| Model | Key fields |
|---|---|
| `User` | `companyId[]`, `role[]`, `email`, `password` (hashed), `avatar`, `favoriteArticles[]` |
| `Article` | `companyId`, `authorId`, `status` (Draft/Pending/Approved/Rejected), `department[]`, `tags[]`, `contentEmbedding[]`, `upvotes[]`, `downvotes[]`, `feedback[]` |
| `Company` | `name`, `emailDomain`, `isActive` |
| `Notification` | `userId`, notification payload |
| `SessionLog` | Admin audit records |

---

## Common pitfalls to avoid

1. **`companyId` is an array** — always use `$in` in queries and `.some()` for access checks.
2. **`role` is an array** — always use `.includes()`.
3. **No `require()`** — project is full ESM. Use `import`.
4. **`contentEmbedding` is `select: false`** — must explicitly select it when needed.
5. **Error handling** — set `res.status()` before `throw new Error()`, not after.
6. **Atlas Vector Search** requires a manually created index named `vector_index` on the `articles` collection.
7. **CORS** — allowed origins are configured in `server/app.js`. Add new origins there, not elsewhere.
